title: a find that discards its errors reads an unreadable directory as an empty one: infra profiles says no domain is claimed twice, and devbin's own syntax gate passes, over trees they could not read
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 by cc, reviewing vc's series, from a census of every `find` under lib/ and bin/ at 2b9d1a5. Issue 0127 fixes the reads of the vendored set (lib/install's two and lib/cmd/doctor:286) and 0131's point 7 fixes clean's scan. (This body first credited lib/helpers:1010 to 0127 too; it is runtime_digest, which 0127 does not touch, and it is point 9 below.) These are the rest of the class: a `find` whose errors go to /dev/null, and whose status is read by nobody, so a directory it could not read is a directory with nothing in it, and the caller reports a complete answer over part of the tree. IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001's shape. vc asked that one issue take the class, with one source arm and one builder, cc.

DRIVEN, each against a control, in a clone of 341ded1:

1. `infra profiles` (lib/cmd/infra.d/profiles:102). Two profiles under one directory, `a/` and `locked/b/`, each claiming x.example. THE CONTROL, readable: refused, exit 1, "x.example claimed by 2 profiles", both files named. With `locked/` at mode 000: exit 0, "1 profile(s) under <dir>, no domain claimed twice." The one check the verb exists for is reported clean over half the estate.
2. devbin's own shell gate (bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/shell-gate:61, `find bin lib tests -type f 2>/dev/null`). A file with a syntax error planted at lib/zzprobe/bad. THE CONTROL, readable: `bin/devbin check syntax` exits 1, "syntax: 48 file(s), 1 breach(es)". With lib/zzprobe at mode 000: exit 0, "syntax: 47 file(s), 0 breach(es)". A gate reporting green over a file it never read. Its "examined NO files" guard cannot see this, since 47 is not 0.
3. `cargo_target_dirs` (lib/helpers:776). A project with `target/` and `locked/sub/target/`. THE CONTROL: both listed, rc 0. With `locked/` at mode 000, under `set -euo pipefail`: only `target/` is printed, and the caller ends with status 1 and no word, since the piped find fails before the function's `return 0`. Its one caller, fullcycle's release check (lib/cmd/fullcycle:671), reads it through a process substitution, so there the list is simply shorter, and a tree beneath what find could not read is never checked for a release binary.

READ, NOT DRIVEN:

4. `infra mail dmarc parse` over a directory (lib/cmd/infra.d/mail.d/dmarc:534): a report beneath an unreadable directory is never parsed, and the summary's counts say nothing of it.
5. fullcycle's PATH-link watch (lib/cmd/fullcycle:195): a PATH directory it cannot read has its links unwatched, so a link the cycle darkens there is not reported.
6. `new` (lib/cmd/new:137), looking for a tests directory, and `check`'s OTP version (lib/cmd/check:410), where a fallback follows. Smaller.
7. lib/cmd/check:313 is the other half of the shape: find's error reaches the screen, but its status is lost in a process substitution, so the swift format check can pass over a partial file list.
8. lib/helpers:2097 is harmless, and needs only a comment saying so: a failure there re-runs the update check.
9. runtime_digest (lib/helpers:1010), found by this issue's own source arm: the seam digest is taken over find's listing of the runtime with its errors sent to /dev/null, so a runtime with a file find could not read digests as a different runtime, with no word of why. Read, not driven.
10. lib/install's seam check (the symlink scan, `links="$(find ...)"`) is the other exception: it reads find's status and reports UNREADABLE, the seam's own answer for a cell it could not vouch for, so only find's text is hidden. It is marked with its reason rather than changed.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO. Each find is read whole with its status, as 0127 and 0131 do, and its own error stays on stderr to name the path. Each caller says the listing is partial and does not report success over it: a gate or a check fails, and a verb that acts may act on what it found and still exit non-zero, as clean does. A find kept silent on purpose says why, in a comment. A source arm over lib/ and bin/ finds every find whose errors are discarded and fails on each one that carries no stated reason, with a positive control that a planted one is found. Pages that describe these commands change where their behaviour does.

cc's. It ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling.

## Resolution

Fixed at b33b34a. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. Each find the issue names is read whole with its status, and its error stays on stderr to name the path. A gate or a check refuses a partial listing, and a verb that acts may act on what it found and still says so: infra profiles and dmarc parse refuse, devbin's own syntax, lint and critic gates refuse a corpus they could not list whole, check format swift fails, fullcycle's artefact check and PATH watch fail the cycle, the runtime digest reads UNREADABLE, check autotests refuses a verdict, and new says its search was partial and goes on. The reviews added: -ignore_readdir_race on the walks a build runs beside, and Swift's build directories pruned in both twins; an artefact check that names a tree it cannot reach or search, or a profile it cannot list, calls a tree gone only when it resolves the path a name at a time, each link followed, and a directory it can search says a name is not there, and names a tree behind a link it cannot follow as that, examines a target/ that is a link as the directory it names, once, counts the trees it examined apart from those it found, and says INCONCLUSIVE only over a walk that read every tree; find -H where a start point may be a link (the runtime's lib, a crate's tests/); check autotests counting a crate's test targets by cargo's own rule, asked of each undotted entry of tests/ as cargo asks it, so a capitalised Main.rs counts where the disk folds case, directory targets and links included; one step for every walk of links, link_step, which follow_links and the artefact check take, and which refuses a link's content it cannot read back exactly under BSD's or GNU's readlink; a runtime digest that reads each file's status and prints only a whole digest; one helper, find_list, for a listing read whole, which check's Swift gate, dmarc parse and check autotests call; a find kept quiet on purpose says why in a `# find-status:` mark; and assert_find_denied, which reads find's error in BSD's form and in GNU's, under the C locale and under UTF-8. A source arm reads every find under lib/ and bin/ and fails on one that loses its error or its status without a mark. The pages say each of these.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD. BSD find passes in silence over a directory it can list but not search, mode 0444 or 0644, below its start point, so every walk here that descends, clean's excepted, still reads the tree beneath one as absent at rc 0. That is 0145, filed into 0.1.8 on vc's ruling with one detector for every such walk; this change does not close it. The critic's I1 for shell_files -- a file that vanishes between the listing and its read -- is head's status rather than find's and is recorded for vc's parked list, as is fullcycle's inline artefact verdict. Declared in the code and on the page rather than closed: the artefact check does not enter a directory that is itself a link, and a link inside the runtime's lib is neither followed nor digested. W4(i), a PATH entry that is a link to a directory, is 0134's. The artefact check reads a relative CARGO_TARGET_DIR from the project root, where cargo reads it from its own working directory, and splits one holding a newline into two paths, both older than 0139; they are 0148, filed into 0.1.8.
- REVIEWS. critic-shell's seven passes: the first on v1 (0 critical, 5 warnings, 7 recommendations), the second on v2d (0 critical, 2 warnings, 6 recommendations, 8 style), the third on v2e's delta (0 critical, 0 warnings, 2 recommendations, 10 style), the fourth on v2f's (0 critical, 0 warnings, 2 recommendations, 10 style), and, under vc's convergence rule, the fifth on v2g's (2 warnings, one a driven false green; v2h) and on v2h's (3 warnings, one a false green; v2i), the sixth on v2i's (2 warnings, one a false green under GNU's readlink; v2j), and the seventh on v2j's (0 critical, 0 warnings, 3 recommendations, 1 style, taken); each point built or answered, and the commit message names each with the pass that raised it. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-25, approved at v2j. Seven critic-shell passes, the last three under vc's convergence rule, where only a critical, a warning or a false green reopens the change; v2j's pass found none of the three, driven under BSD and GNU readlink with BSD and GNU find. vc confirmed the 115 mutant verdicts itself from the results (0 not killed), approved the v2i and v2j plans, and ruled out of 0139 what is older than it: the relative and newline CARGO_TARGET_DIR (0148) and the directory find can list and not search (0145), each filed into 0.1.8.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. v1's ten arms were red at its base. v2's were red on v1's code where they hold new behaviour and on the base without 0139 where they hold 0139's, each at its own assertion, and each later review's arms on the code that review read; those green by construction are held by mutants. 115 mutants, each against its own arm after every killer ran green on the unmutated tree: 115 of 115 killed (2026-09-25, 11:22:31Z to 11:28:03Z); one dropped as equivalent with the code it mutated removed, and two refusals in link_step declared equivalent alone in its comment.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the nine 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on b10dd41, 0139 first, on a clean checkout (head 308cf21), 2026-09-25 11:34:20Z to 12:09:20Z: 1907 of 1907 ok, 0 not ok, no gaps, its 5 skips the suite's declared ones. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree outside intent/.
